claims.text: Controlled post-deposition oxidation can form a continuous, adherent oxide scale on an FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating.
A continuous, adherent oxide scale will improve the high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu relative to an as-deposited coating.
An FeNiCrCoCu coating deposited under inert conditions is non-oxidized in its baseline state.
The baseline coating exhibits a typical microstructure and grain size associated with standard deposition.
Annealing in a controlled, mildly oxidizing atmosphere will induce surface-oxide-scale formation.
The pre-formed oxide scale limits direct metal-to-metal contact during high-temperature sliding.
The pre-formed oxide scale suppresses further oxidation of the coating during wear.
The pre-formed oxide scale reduces adhesive wear.
The oxide barrier inhibits abrasive wear.
The oxide barrier inhibits chemical attack.
Oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings under otherwise identical high-temperature wear tests.
Oxidized coatings will exhibit less material loss than as-deposited coatings.
Oxidized coatings will exhibit lower friction than as-deposited coatings.
The predicted wear benefit applies in a high-temperature regime around 500°C.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis concerns improved wear resistance, while the falsification rule appears to require improvement in both wear rate and friction. Failure to reduce friction alone would not necessarily contradict the stated wear-resistance hypothesis.

Absence of a continuous oxide layer after treatment is treated as falsification, although it may instead indicate that the intended mediator was never successfully produced; a decisive mechanism test should confirm oxide formation before judging its effect on wear.
